sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Jamestown, NY?
sections.html:
Selling in Jamestown means working in one of the least expensive housing markets in New York: the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $87,700 for 2020-2024. That is a fraction of values downstate, so a repair bill of a few thousand dollars can change a sale more here than it would elsewhere.

The city had an estimated 27,663 residents on July 1, 2025, down 3.6% from the 2020 base of 28,698. It peaked at 45,155 in the 1930 census and has fallen in every census since 1950. Just under half of housing units are owner-occupied (49.3%), so many sellers are landlords as well as homeowners. The 2020-2024 figures show 12,602 households and 2.19 people per household.

  • Owner-occupants selling a family home often face deferred maintenance, since median monthly owner costs run $974 with a mortgage and $472 without.
  • Landlords selling a rental must watch the city's registration and inspection rules.
  • Heirs and out-of-town owners often sell a vacant house and want a quick close.

sections.h2: Where is Jamestown and what shaped its housing?
sections.html:
Jamestown is in Chautauqua County at the eastern tip of Chautauqua Lake, with the Chadakoin River running through it. It lies 71 miles southwest of Buffalo and 145 miles northeast of Cleveland, and it became a village in 1827 and a city on April 19, 1886.

The city grew on the furniture, worsted and metal trades, and the area was once called the furniture capital of the world. Its population climbed from 3,155 in 1860 to 45,155 in 1930. Cummins runs a diesel engine plant in the neighboring Town of Busti, six miles away, and Wikipedia describes it as the largest single employer in the city, with more than 1,500 employees. UPMC Chautauqua is the regional hospital, and Census data shows health care and social assistance receipts of about $315.6 million in 2022.

The National Comedy Center opened on August 1, 2018, partly in the former Erie Railroad station, and the city is the hometown of Lucille Ball. For a seller, these draw visitors but mostly affect downtown and nearby streets rather than the whole city.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Jamestown's housing market?
sections.html:
Jamestown's median household income is $43,523 for 2020-2024, per-capita income is $26,557, and 25.3% of residents live in poverty. Median gross rent is $759. Those figures frame what local buyers can afford to pay.

The city covers 8.90 square miles of land, and mean travel time to work is only 15.2 minutes. 87.2% of adults hold a high school diploma or higher and 21.3% hold a bachelor's degree. About 20.3% of residents under 65 report a disability, so a first-floor bedroom or a ramp is worth stating in a listing. The 2020 census counted 14,430 housing units, of which 12.4% were vacant, and a rental vacancy rate of 10.2%.

Buyers have choices when more than one in ten units sits empty. If you need to sell within weeks, price against nearby sales rather than a number that works downstate, and expect a buyer to ask what repairs the house needs.

sections.h2: What do landlords and sellers need to do under Jamestown's rental rules?
sections.html:
Jamestown requires every owner of residential rental units to file a Landlord Registration Form with the City Clerk each year by February 1, and a new owner must file within 30 days of a transfer. The rule comes from Chapter 215 of the Jamestown City Code and applies to every recorded owner of a property with rental units or rooms.

The program is aimed at substandard housing and keeps a log of available units for emergency response. Exemptions cover transient lodging, state-licensed hospitals and hospices, religious housing, and units that a government agency inspects at least every five years. A rental registration must list the parcel number, the number of units, owner contact details, a local contact representative, repair-request contact information and violations from the past two years.

This matters in a sale because the buyer of a rental inherits a 90-day inspection of the exterior, common areas and every unit. A seller who discloses open code issues up front keeps the deal on track. Tenant consent is needed for unit inspections, and the city may seek a court warrant if access is refused. Registration forms go to the City Clerk at 200 East Third Street, Municipal Building, first floor.

sections.h2: How does Jamestown code enforcement affect a sale?
sections.html:
Code enforcement in the city's Department of Development applies Chapter 215, the Property Maintenance and Conservation Code, and an open violation can follow the property into a sale. Officers investigate complaints, photograph conditions and issue either a Notice of Violation or an Appearance Ticket to City Court.

An Appearance Ticket goes out automatically for junk and debris, high grass and weeds, infestations and unregistered vehicles. A Notice of Violation covers items such as peeling paint, and it carries a compliance deadline plus photographs. If nothing is done, the city moves to an Appearance Ticket. Residents report concerns through the GovPilot system or the GovAlert app.

Before listing, walk the exterior for the items on that list. Cutting grass, hauling debris and repainting peeling trim cost little and remove the most common reasons a buyer's attorney pauses a deal. Vacant or abandoned buildings are one of the categories residents can report through GovAlert, so keep a vacant inherited house maintained.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Chautauqua County, and what do the taxes come to?
sections.html:
A Jamestown deed is recorded with the Chautauqua County Clerk, which charges a $50 statutory fee plus $5 for each additional page. A mandatory $10 notice of transfer, a $5 TP-584 filing fee and the RP-5217 filing fee of $125 for residential and agricultural property are added to that.

Transfer tax in the county is $4.00 for the first $1,000 of consideration and then $2.00 per $500 after that. Half goes to New York State and half to Chautauqua County. The clerk's example shows that a price of $150,500 produces tax of $602, and one dollar more raises it to $604. On a sale at the city's $87,700 median value, the tax would be about $352 by the clerk's formula.

The clerk rejects deeds that lack a legal description, the full names and physical addresses of the grantor and grantee, or the grantor's original notarized signature. White-out and redaction are not allowed; the clerk recommends drawing a fresh deed instead of correcting one. Credit-card payments of $20 or more carry a 2.5% processing fee. Out-of-state sellers need form IT-2663 with the deed.

sections.h2: When should a Jamestown owner consider a cash offer?
sections.html:
A cash offer is worth comparing when the house is vacant, needs more repair than the price can absorb, or sits in a registered rental portfolio the owner wants to exit.

Ask the buyer whether the offer includes the registration and 90-day inspection duties that follow a transfer of a rental, and whether any open Chapter 215 violations would be cleared by the seller or the buyer. Winter timing also matters: Jamestown averages 98.4 inches of snow a year, with 46.6 snowy days, so roof and heating problems found in January can reshape a deal. Have a New York attorney read the contract before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental in Jamestown after I buy or sell it?
faqs.a: Yes. A new owner must file the Landlord Registration Form with the City Clerk within 30 days of the transfer, and all owners file by February 1 each year. The form is required by Chapter 215 of the city code, and failure to file can lead to legal action and court costs.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in Chautauqua County?
faqs.a: The tax is $4.00 for the first $1,000 of consideration and $2.00 for each $500 after that, split equally between New York State and the county. On a $150,500 sale it comes to $602, according to the County Clerk's own example.

faqs.q: How many people live in Jamestown, NY?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 27,663 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is a 3.6% drop from the April 2020 estimates base of 28,698, and well below the 1930 peak of 45,155.

faqs.q: Will the city inspect a rental after I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental properties are subject to inspection within 90 days of an ownership transfer, covering the exterior, common areas and every rental unit. The city mails written notice 14 days ahead, and a failure to comply leads to revocation of the Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: What can hold up a Jamestown house sale at the County Clerk?
faqs.a: A deed can be rejected for a missing legal description, missing addresses or an unsigned or un-notarized grantor signature. Redactions and white-out are not accepted. The clerk also needs the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms, and out-of-state sellers add form IT-2663.
